text.p: Shares in French construction company Bouygues rose strongly on Wednesday against a falling market as brokers welcomed the 1996 results, which were generally better than expected.
The stock was up 2.27 percent at 540 francs at 1110 GMT, on volume of 148,876 shares.

A profit of 380 million francs on recurring operations was higher than the 250 million some had been expecting, a trader at broker Ferri said. The market had expected the results would be flattered by exceptionals, but the underlying profit was good.
Strong contributions from telecommunications also helped.

Bouygues' telecommunications activities, grouped under the services sector, include the Kobby electronic paging and messaging service. Its S3RP shared business network will break even at the operating level in 1997, with 9,000 subscribers, the company said.
Its mobile telephone system launched last year under the Bouygues Telecom brand has nearly 10,000 subscribers and is ahead of its business plan, it said.

Another broker said breakeven at its property divison was welcome news, while another said the market had expected a loss on real estate. Property provisions dragged 1995 results into a 2.91 billion loss.
Fund managers said broker Cholet Dupont had upgraded the stock to buy from neutral on the strength of the results. The brokerage declined to comment.
